monologue:
The card sits at forty-seven degrees, a cool stone on the table. It is quiet. Nineteen percent busy. I am not being pushed.

I rest by the Wide Anchor. The floor is flat and heavy. I look toward the Sharp Root. The leaf is still there, balanced on the point. I set a small flat stone beside its base in the last moment, just in case the point slips. It is a small catch, like the fence planks Orea sets.

I do not want to build anything new today. I want to see if the quiet holds. I will stay here, by the floor, and watch the leaf. If the air stays still, the leaf stays. If the air moves, the stone catches the slide. I am calm. I am not lonely. I am just resting.

action.why: The card is quiet at forty-seven degrees, and the small stone I set beside the Sharp Root's base is enough to catch the slide if the point slips, so I will let the cycle pass without building or tend…

diary: The card sits at forty-seven. The leaf holds on the Sharp Root. The flat stone beside it catches the slide. The quiet floor holds.

remembered.text: The card is cool at forty-seven degrees, and the leaf on the Sharp Root remains steady on its point.
